title.en: Johnny Cash Announces that Stitches is Hostile Again in WoW: Forever
title.es: Johnny Cash anuncia que Stitches vuelve a ser hostil en WoW: Forever

summary.en: Johnny Cash Announces that Stitches is Hostile Again in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Johnny Cash anuncia que Stitches vuelve a ser hostil en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
Johnny Cash has announced on X (Twitter) that Stitches is hostile in WoW: Forever once again.

Stitches is one of the most famous NPCs in WoW: Classic. Found in Duskwood, he patrols the road, striking down anyone who gets too close. During last week's Beta build, players noticed that Stitches was marked as a neutral mob, and this has now been fixed, according to Johnny Cash on X (Twitter).

Tweet #2107204533944504382


If you're entering Duskwood, make sure to watch out for an angry Stitches!

contentHtml:
Blizzard has released a new video on their World of Warcraft YouTube Channel breaking down who the Skyborne are, their origins, their unique racials, and what classes they can be.



A pinned comment from the channel itself announces that we will learn more information about the Skyborne models, which has been one of the hottest topics so far regarding World of Warcraft: Forever. Currently, the Skyborne are the only race in-game that have no proper Standard Definition models, along with their Druid form models as well.

author: Wowhead Staff

title.en: What's Best for WoW: Forever - Party Buffs or Raid Buffs?
title.es: ¿Qué es lo mejor para WoW: Forever - Party Mejoras o Banda Mejoras?

summary.en: What's Best for WoW: Forever - Party Buffs or Raid Buffs?...
summary.es: ¿Qué es lo mejor para WoW: Forever - Party Mejoras o Banda Mejoras?...

contentHtml:
In Vanilla WoW and The Burning Crusade, powerful buffs such as a Warrior's Battle Shout, a Feral Druid's Leader of the Pack, and a Shaman's Windfury Totem are only available to those in the party of the class or spec offering it. In Wrath of the Lich King and beyond, these buffs were made available to everyone in a raid as well, not just a party. WoW: Forever follows the Vanilla/TBC formula of party-wide buffs, but would it be better for players if these buffs were raid-wide instead?

Party Buffs or Raid Buffs?

Party buffs, as we saw in TBC and Vanilla, made it so that players had to bring a variety of classes and specs to their raid team to fully enhance every member of each party. A melee group would have one Feral Druid for Leader of the Pack, one Warrior for Battle Shout, one to two Beastmastery Hunters or Ret Paladins for Ferocious Inspiration/Improved Sanctity Aura, and one Enhancement Shaman for Windfury Totem or Grace of Air Totem.


A Standard "Meta" TBC Raid Team


Because you typically have more than one melee group, this ensures that at least two of each class and spec mentioned above have to be brought into the raid, preventing raid teams from stacking the best DPS class or spec if buffs were raid-wide. If an Enhancement Shaman was the lowest DPS class in the game and buffs were raid-wide, you could only bring one, or potentially none if a Restoration Shaman could drop Windfury for them!

Windfury Totem
250 Mana
Instant
Requires Shaman
Requires level 52
Tools:
Air Totem
Summons a Windfury Totem with 5 health at the feet of the caster. The totem enhances the melee attacks of all party members within 30 yards. Each main hand hit has a 20% chance of granting the attacker 1 extra attack with [(246 * 1)]246 extra melee attack power. Lasts 5 min.


However, this poses a problem with party buffs that gets easily solved if all buffs were raid-wide instead. Players who recently played TBC Anniversary realized that some buffs, such as a Shaman's Windfury Totem, are so incredibly powerful that not having it is a genuine gameplay difference. A Warrior's overall DPS and APM is significantly affected by not having this buff. So there are two problems: a class can play completely differently without certain buffs, and now raid team compositions become incredibly one-dimensional and restricted.


5 Shamans in TBC felt like a requirement for every raid team to have 


The latter is a big issue, especially for PUG raids. A PUG raid leader may find themselves looking for an extended period of time to find that class or spec to meet their buff needs, and because of that, take away time they have in the raid. If buffs were raid-wide, then you significantly decrease the restrictions that a raid team would have trying to meet the buff needs for every party. Party buffs and their meta raid compositions to follow tend to bleed more into the general population compared to the problem created by raid-wide buffs: "Class Stacking."


A raid team in Wrath of the Lich King Stacking Unholy Death Knights


"Class Stacking" is when, after you've filled every necessary raid buff slot, you can then fill the rest of the slot with one specific class/spec - often the one that just theoretically deals the most damage. You would see this in expansions like Wrath of the Lich King, where top teams would stack as many Unholy Death Knights as possible to maximize their raid DPS once they filled the necessary roles. So the problem now arises here when raid leaders start saying something along the lines of "okay, we found our one Shaman, now we don't need to invite any more!"

What's Best For WoW Forever?

With both having their pros and cons, we have to ask: what would be best for Forever? "Main" raids in WoW: Forever seem to lean towards the 10- and 20-man raids, where 40-man raids seem to be more of a novelty and "quick raids" compared to the length of the other two sizes. With 20-man raids being the biggest size for the longer raids, would party or raid buffs be better?



Comparing the cons from both, we have restricted raid compositions with party buffs versus potential class stacking with raid buffs. When analyzing these cons, a phrase that players tend to counter each with is "you don't need to do this to clear the content". And this is true: you don't need to have a Shaman in every raid in TBC to clear the raids (although after raiding with one, you definitely never want to raid without one), and you certainly don't need to class stack to clear all the raids in Wrath of the Lich King. But when we look at both and consider a 20-man raid composition, raid buffs may potentially be better overall for WoW Forever.


A standard 20-player raid composition if buffs were party-wide only


If WoW: Forever sticks with party buffs, a meta raid composition could potentially lock in up to seventeen of the twenty slots available. If Forever converted all party buffs to be raid-wide, then only twelve of those slots would be needed to fill all the buffs. With 10-man raids, you can now cover buffs with 10 fewer people as well.


A standard 20-player raid composition if buffs were raid-wide


When also looking at the fear of class-stacking, although this was something that happens with raid buffs, it's only really apparent in groups who compete for rankings in Warcraft Logs - whereas party buff raid comps definitely seem to bleed more into the general population of raid teams. A trade chat pug often struggles to fill a raid team to meet all the specific party buff needs. With raid-wide buffs, this definitely makes filling a pug group much easier. If Forever raid content avoids DPS checks as a raid encounter, then it's highly unlikely we'll see class stacking as a problem.



Blizzard has stated in their latest podcast that they plan to look at buffs such as Shaman Totems and whether they should stay party-wide, so perhaps we may be given an update on buffs in raids or parties before the game goes live on November 4th.

title.en: WoW: Forever Character Creation Portraits Now Have SD and HD Versions
title.es: WoW: Los retratos de creación de personajes de Forever ahora tienen versiones SD y HD

summary.en: WoW: Forever Character Creation Portraits Now Have SD and HD Versions...
summary.es: WoW: Los retratos de creación de personajes para siempre ahora tienen versiones SD y HD...

contentHtml:
Players noticed that the character creation screen in WoW: Forever only had the High Definition/Retail portraits for all the races, even when the Standard Definition/Classic toggle was on. In a recent build, it appears Blizzard has now added back the SD portraits after popular demand.


High Definition Character Creation Screen

Standard Definition Character Creation Screen


Players who opt into Classic toggles in WoW Forever have been very passionate when certain features, systems, or parts of the UI are actually what they looked like in Classic. Content creators such as Xaryu have been heavily advocating for Blizzard to add a full Classic toggle for the entire UI in WoW: Forever as well. With Blizzard listening to player feedback on the character creation screen, it shows that they are very open to feedback and responding to popular requests as the beta progresses.

title.es: Las profesiones obtienen divertidos bonos de equipo temático en WoW: Forever

contentHtml:
Professions have gotten a ton of new recipes, bonuses, and even gear in WoW: Forever - including dungeon pieces that increase crafting speed and hammers that double as throwing weapons!

New Crafting Gear Bonuses in WoW Forever

Players have noticed a couple of updated pieces in the Deadmines dungeon, with items like Smelting Pants, and now, after this latest build, Cookie's Stirring Rod. The former is great for early-level Miners, but the latter is something all wand users can use throughout for that increased cooking speed.

Another fun crafting-related piece of gear is the Arcanite Blacksmith Hammer, a throwing weapon that has a chance on hit to stun the target. However, this item, as the tooltip reads, also serves as a Blacksmith Hammer. Carrying around a traditional Blacksmith Hammer always feels like a required bag slot filled up, but once you're able to craft this thrown weapon, you can toss out that old hammer for this powerful upgrade.

Items such as these create a fun farm for players to obtain upgrades to their character that don't necessarily always upgrade their player power, which is exactly the kind of horizontal progression that WoW: Forever is looking to provide.

title.en: Student Fodder Doesn't Give Rested Experience in WoW: Forever
title.es: Student Fodder no ofrece experiencia en WoW: Forever

summary.en: Student Fodder Doesn't Give Rested Experience in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Student Fodder no ofrece experiencia en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
Season of Discovery's Sleeping Bag quest chain makes a return in WoW: Forever. One of the rewards from the quest chain, Student Fodder, would give players four bars of rested experience. In WoW: Forever, though, this buff has been removed and replaced with new effects.

How To Get The Sleeping Bag In WoW: Forever 


The Student Fodder's buff in WoW Forever will still instantly heal and replenish a portion of your class's resource bar, but now it also applies Trail Snack, a 60% speed boost for .75 seconds. The base buff, Trail Snack, now also heals the player over time for 175 per tick as well.



It could be assumed that the removal of the rested experience buff comes with the fact that we have, so far, three other ways to increase leveling speed for players. When players rest at a campfire, they'll be granted one bar of rested experience that you can get every hour, almost all new food buffs provide a 5% experience buff, and the Cozy Sleeping Bag itself grants players up to a +3% experience buff for an hour. On top of that, Legacy talents will also make leveling easier for alts, so perhaps SoD's Student Fodder would be seen as too much for expediting the leveling journey.
